about: The repaired ATC answer key (docs/SIMILARITY-LITERATURE.md, step 1). Questions are the molecules with an N code, as in the headline key; peers are read from every ATC code the catalogue holds, at any anatomical level. A level-4 class whose fifth character is X is dropped as before, and so is every class below, each for the reason given: it is a residual group, a group by use or indication, or not a pharmacological group at all, so membership in it says nothing about how a drug acts. A level-3 group listed under excluded_level3 gives no sibling credit, for the same reason. A change to this file is a change of instrument: bump the version, say why in docs/SIMILARITY-HARNESS.md, and never make it in the same change as a scoring constant it judges.

excluded_level4.N02BG: residual: 'Other analgesics and antipyretics' (nefopam, ziconotide, flupirtine, tanezumab, ...), the junk drawer the X rule exists to drop, filed under another letter
excluded_level4.N05CM: residual: 'Other hypnotics and sedatives' (dexmedetomidine, methaqualone, scopolamine, clomethiazole, ...), as N02BG
excluded_level4.A01AD: residual: 'Other agents for local oral treatment'
excluded_level4.J04AK: residual: 'Other drugs for treatment of tuberculosis'
excluded_level4.N07BA: use: 'Drugs used in nicotine dependence'. Its three members here (nicotine, cytisinicline, varenicline) happen to share nicotinic agonism, but the class is defined by use, and a key that keeps a use class wherever it happens to agree with mechanism is being chosen by its answers
excluded_level4.N07BB: use: 'Drugs used in alcohol dependence' puts disulfiram, acamprosate and carbimide beside naltrexone and nalmefene
excluded_level4.N07BC: use: 'Drugs used in opioid dependence' puts lofexidine, an alpha-2 agonist, beside methadone and buprenorphine
excluded_level4.N07CA: use: 'Antivertigo preparations' puts betahistine beside cinnarizine and flunarizine
excluded_level4.V03AB: use: 'Antidotes' puts naloxone, flumazenil, physostigmine and acetylcysteine together (SIMILARITY-DIAGNOSIS §1)
excluded_level4.G04BD: use: 'Drugs for urinary frequency and incontinence'
excluded_level4.G04BE: use: 'Drugs used in erectile dysfunction' puts apomorphine and yohimbine beside the PDE5 inhibitors
excluded_level4.C05BB: not pharmacological: 'Sclerosing agents for local injection'

excluded_level3.N02B: residual: 'Other analgesics and antipyretics' groups salicylates, paracetamol and gabapentinoids

not_excluded_on_purpose.route classes: A class that groups by route but whose members share one mechanism (S01HA, C05AD, D04AB local anaesthetics; M02AA topical NSAIDs) stays: a peer found through it acts the same way.
not_excluded_on_purpose.level-3 X groups: A level-3 group whose fourth character is X ('other ...') gives no sibling credit, by rule rather than by listing; its level-4 classes are kept where they name one mechanism (G03XC, selective estrogen receptor modulators).
not_excluded_on_purpose.structure classes: The chemical-structure classes (N02AA-N02AF, N05AA-N05AL, ...) stay, because removing them would remove most of the key; their splits are what the level-3 sibling credit answers.
